title: VIDEO: NJ Mother and Daughter Cling to Robbers' Car as Thieves Flee With $1M in Gold
text: Headlines VIDEO: NJ Mother and Daughter Cling to Robbers’ Car as Thieves Flee With $1M in Gold “Brave” intervention leaves owners injured and distraught following smash and grab that wiped out their uninsured inventory. Published 2 days ago on April 9, 2026 By INSTORE Staff Share Tweet Police are searching for a crew of masked bandits who stole an estimated $1 million in gold from a family-run jewelry store in Perth Amboy, NJ, on Wednesday, as the owners were filmed desperately clinging to the getaway vehicle. The robbery occurred around 3 p.m. at SD Jewelry on Madison Avenue when four or five suspects used sledgehammers to smash through the front window. Video footage shows the thieves stuffing gold jewelry into trash bags before fleeing to a BMW SUV with Illinois license plates. Co-owner Stephanie Duran and her mother confronted the thieves, clinging to the vehicle’s doors and clothing as it reversed. “I said to my mom ‘they’re not going to take all my effort,’” Duran told ABC7, adding she previously worked as an Uber driver until 5 a.m. to save money for the business. Duran’s mother suffered bruises to her arms and legs after being thrown to the ground as the car sped away. “She fought with them like a man. She’s a brave woman,” witness Jessie Sanchez told the New York Post. Perth Amboy Police Chief Larry Cattano told CBS New York that officers arrived within 25 seconds of a 911 call, but the call was placed after the suspects fled. Family member Perla Ceballos told News 12 that the shop lacked insurance for the $1 million loss because the monthly premiums were too expensive. No arrests have been made as of Thursday.
